title: Wantagh High School: Indigenous Mascot Debate
summary: Wantagh’s ongoing Warrior-name dispute connects school identity with Native calls for respectful representation. In February 2026, the district announced a compliance extension to June 2027.
address_label: Wantagh High School, 3297 Beltagh Avenue, Wantagh, NY
ancestral_territory_note: Contemporary Indigenous representation in the Merrick–Wantagh area.
why_this_matters: A student newspaper’s disagreement over the Wantagh mascot brings Indigenous representation into an everyday public institution. Reading that debate alongside Native Nations’ recorded support for change connects school traditions with the people those traditions claim to represent.
introduction_title: A Debate in the Student Newspaper
introduction_content: On February 13, 2023, sports editor Michelle Smith argued in Wantagh High School’s The Warrior that Indigenous mascots should be retired. Her opinion article also described petitions and social-media opposition within the school community.
history_title: Native Nations and the Statewide Discussion
history_content:
New York State Education Department’s 2023 assessment of public comments records support for its proposed Indigenous-mascot prohibition from the Shinnecock Indian Nation and Oneida Indian Nation. The department also distinguished retiring stereotypes from erasing history, supporting accurate teaching about Native cultures.

Update: February 2026

In its February 10, 2026 letter, the Wantagh Board of Education announced that NYSED had extended its compliance deadline to June 30, 2027. The board said students would continue under the Warrior name while the district pursued state litigation and a federal appeal.

The district has advocated keeping the Warrior name with rebranded imagery. Native Nations’ support for the statewide changes places the voices of the people represented by these traditions at the center of the debate.
whereintheworld_content: Wantagh High School is on Beltagh Avenue. School grounds follow district access rules.
